purpose: Lexical candidates for human review only. A match means a configured phrase occurred; it does not establish meaning, scope, speaker, entailment, completeness, permission or acceptance.
construction_policy: Every cue string attested in the dev fixture gold (fixtures/dev.jsonl).
Every example word in the topic table of fixtures/ANNOTATION.md (frozen with the reserved set as the topic specification).

Closed-class completions only: English and Spanish negators, English central modals, third-person present/conditional/future forms of Spanish deber, poder and tener que, typographic apostrophe variants, accent variants.
Nothing else: no expression attested only in the reserved set was added. The rule author also wrote the reserved set and cannot forget it; see README limitations.

notes: Also introduces indirect questions ('ask if', 'whether').
Inside 'only if', 'as if', 'even if' the meaning differs; overlapping matches are all reported.
Necessary-condition reading; the nested 'if' is also reported.
Can be read as a condition or as an exception.
'provided' alone (without 'that') is not configured.
Also temporal or comparative ('as long as the table').
Also a verb ('to except').
The nested 'except' is also reported.
Also plain comparison ('other than expected').
Also in fixed expressions without negative meaning ('not only ... but also', 'whether or not').
Also the abbreviation 'No.' (number) and fixed expressions ('no longer', 'no doubt').
'neither' and 'nor' also join alternatives.
Often a preposition of absence rather than clausal negation.
The ability/permission modal inside it is not reported separately.
Matched only as a suffix attached to a word ('isn't', 'can't'); the host auxiliary is not reported by this rule.
Also permission ('you may enter'); permission is never inferred.
Case-insensitive: also matches the month name 'May'.
Also the noun 'might' (strength) and past/polite permission.
Also past ability or polite request.
'likely' is also an adjective ('a likely place').
Also 'according to plan/size' (conformity, no source).
The speaker or source is never identified.
'reported' also as adjective; 'claims' also as noun.
Also epistemic inference ('it must be late').
Also future or offers ('shall we').
Deontic or epistemic ('it should arrive soon').
Also 'have to do with' (relation); other persons and tenses are not configured.
Also indirect questions ('pregunta si'), the musical note, and 'sí' (yes) written without its accent.
A decomposed 'sí' (s, i, U+0301) does not match: a combining mark after the cue blocks the right boundary.
'en caso de' without 'que' is not configured.
'a salvo' means 'safe'.
In 'salvo que' it introduces an exceptive condition; only 'salvo' is reported.
Also inside non-negative fixed expressions ('no obstante' = nevertheless) and the abbreviation 'n.º'/'No.'.
'nada' is also a form of the verb 'nadar' (swims).
Also intensifier ('ni siquiera') and coordinated 'ni ... ni'.
A preposition of absence; also in fixed expressions ('sin embargo' = however).
Also ability or permission ('se pueden usar'); permission is never inferred.
Also 'según' meaning 'depending on' or 'as' (no source).
Matched as written, NFC or NFD; partially decomposed or compatibility forms do not match.
Also agreement ('estar de acuerdo con') or conformity.
The speaker or source is never identified; other tenses and persons are not configured.
'debe de' can express probability; not distinguished.
Also 'hay que' in 'no hay que' (no need to), which is reported together with the separate 'no'.
